title: Nigerians talented to lead global sports — Shettima
excerpt: Vice President Kashim Shettima says Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports.
description: Vice President Kashim Shettima says Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports.
content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima says Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports.

Shettima said this on Tuesday when he received the newly appointed General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football, Samson Adamu, and the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, at the Presidential Villa, Abuja.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He described the appointment of Adamu as the first Nigerian General Secretary of CAF as additional proof of the country’s potential for international leadership.

Shettima said Nigeria’s sporting achievements had been driven by the quality of its people.

He commended the dedication of sports administrators and the institutions that discover, nurture and project Nigerian talent onto the global stage.

The Vice President congratulated Adamu on his appointment and urged him to distinguish himself through exemplary leadership and service to African football.

“Our nation has earned its place in the world of sports. We have flown our flag in arenas where few expected us to perform magic.

“We have made the impossible appear almost familiar, fundamentally because of the quality of our people,” he said.

Shettima, who conveyed President Bola Tinubu’s goodwill to Adamu, described him as a role model for young Nigerians.

The Vice President urged him to approach his new responsibilities with diligence, integrity and a strong sense of national pride.

He also urged him to promote, protect, project and preserve Nigeria’s interests, while wishing him success.

“Football especially is a uniting force in this country. Anytime Nigeria plays, it tends to subsume all other identities.

“Football and sports generally are a source of unity for our country. What binds us together supersedes whatever divides us,” he stated.

Shettima maintained that Nigeria’s diversity remained a source of strength, stressing that the country’s social and historical bonds were deeper than the divisions sometimes emphasised in public discourse.

He commended the often-unrecognised contributions of officials, coaches, talent scouts and administrators whose work provides the foundation for Nigeria’s sporting achievements.

“The minds that organise, the hands that prepare and the institutions that give talents a fighting chance are always not recognised.

“This is why from the bottom of my heart, on behalf of my Boss, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, we appreciate you,” he said.

He recalled the contributions of Nigerian football legends, including Rashidi Yekini, Austin Jay-Jay Okocha and Finidi George.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Shettima noted that their successes were made possible by individuals and institutions that identified and developed their talents.

Earlier, Dikko thanked the Federal Government for its support for sports development.

He said the administration’s commitment had helped enhance Nigeria’s international sporting profile and attract investment opportunities.

Dikko described Adamu’s appointment as a significant milestone for Nigerian sports administration.

He expressed appreciation for the Federal Government’s approval of Nigeria’s hosting of the CAF General Assembly and CAF Awards in November and December 2026.

According to him, the government’s support for sports had also strengthened the country’s ability to attract international investment through sporting activities and partnerships.

Responding, Adamu described his emergence as the first Nigerian to occupy the position in CAF’s 70-year history as a source of national pride.

Adamu pledged to draw on his experience as CAF’s former Director of Competitions to strengthen the continental football body’s administration and advance the development of African football.

He also expressed his commitment to supporting Nigeria’s efforts to harness its abundant football talent and realise its potential within the continental and global sporting landscape.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Adamu was appointed CAF General Secretary on Sunday, November 1, following a recruitment exercise by the continental football body.

He is expected to oversee CAF’s day-to-day administration.

title: Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister
excerpt: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a firs...
description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a firs...
content:
The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a first-class degree in accounting from the American institution.

Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications.

“I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said.

Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…”

When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.”

He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity.

“Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said.

The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy.

“Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said.

However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements.

“Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added.

Tinubu’s academic qualifications have continued to attract public scrutiny, particularly following the controversy surrounding his Chicago State University records during the 2023 presidential election petition.

The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Tinubu’s Form EC9, sighted by PUNCH, listed a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration from Chicago State University, awarded with honours on June 22, 1979.

The form also listed his National Youth Service Corps discharge documents, indicating that he served in Oyo State from December 1982 to November 1983.

However, the spaces provided for his primary and secondary school qualifications were entered as “0000”, with only his university qualification indicated in the educational history published by the commission.

The development renewed questions about the President’s educational background, with political figures and commentators expressing different views on the omissions.

The university had earlier confirmed that Tinubu attended the institution and graduated in 1979, with accounting as his major.

In September 2023, the university released Tinubu’s academic records following a legal request by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, who sought the documents as part of his challenge to the President’s election victory.

The university’s registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified in a United States court that Tinubu attended and graduated from the institution.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

However, the university’s records confirm accounting as Tinubu’s major but do not specify that he graduated with a first-class classification. The claim that he obtained a first-class degree was made by Alausa during Tuesday’s interview.

In October 2023, a BBC fact-check found no evidence that Tinubu forged the Chicago State University diploma he submitted to INEC.

title: Otti urges teriary students to embrace leadership, integrity, discipline
excerpt: Abia State Governor Alex Otti, has charged students of tertiary institutions in the state to embrace good leadership, integrity, discipline and excellence as critical values nee...
description: Abia State Governor Alex Otti, has charged students of tertiary institutions in the state to embrace good leadership, integrity, discipline and excellence as critical values nee...
content:
Abia State Governor Alex Otti, has charged students of tertiary institutions in the state to embrace good leadership, integrity, discipline and excellence as critical values needed to build a prosperous New Abia.

Otti gave the charge on Tuesday during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Abia State Tertiary Education Sports Fiesta and the official unveiling of the New Abia Crusaders Club at the Umuahia Township Stadium.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The governor, who was represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, said the future of the state depends largely on the quality of character and contributions of its young people.

“The New Abia project is not limited to road construction, school renovation, healthcare improvement and infrastructure development, but is fundamentally about building people, restoring values, creating opportunities and raising a generation committed to excellence, integrity and service,” Otti said.

He described the fiesta as more than a gathering of students, noting that it provides an opportunity to celebrate youthful energy, intellectual excellence and creativity.

“This fiesta is more than a gathering of students. It provides an opportunity to celebrate youthful energy, intellectual excellence, creativity and the enormous potential of young people to contribute to the development of the state,” he stated.

Otti said his administration recognises education as one of the most important investments in the future of Abia and stressed the need for tertiary institutions to become centres of innovation, research and entrepreneurship.

He said his government is committed to producing graduates who are not just certificate holders but problem-solvers and job creators.

“We are committed to producing graduates who will not only possess academic certificates but also become problem-solvers, innovators, employers of labour and responsible citizens capable of competing favourably anywhere in the world,” he added.

The governor described the newly unveiled New Abia Crusaders Club as a platform for cultivating leadership, responsible citizenship and community service among students.

He urged the leadership of the club to organise mentorship programmes, innovation competitions and community development projects.

“I urge the leadership of the club to organise mentorship programmes, academic and innovation competitions, environmental initiatives and community development projects that will make meaningful contributions to society.

“Leadership begins with the choices you make and the positive influence you exert in your communities. Invest in yourselves, uphold your values and become active participants in building the society you desire,” Otti charged the students.

He assured that his administration would continue to place young people at the centre of its development agenda through policies aimed at expanding access to quality education, promoting digital skills and creating opportunities for productive employment.

In her remarks, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Professor Uche Eme-Uche, described the New Abia Crusaders Club as an elite platform across federal, state and private institutions to promote responsible leadership.

“The New Abia Crusaders Club is an elite platform established across federal, state and private tertiary institutions to promote responsible leadership, integrity, service and positive citizenship among students,” Prof. Eme-Uche said.

She highlighted the achievements of the Otti administration in the tertiary education sector, including infrastructural development, improved staff welfare, clearance of inherited salary arrears and restoration of lost accreditations.

“The interventions have created a more conducive environment for teaching, learning, research and innovation. Members of the New Abia Crusaders must be properly informed, guided by good values and committed to making positive contributions to society,” she added.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Also speaking, the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Sir Nwaobilor Ananaba, said sports remains a vital tool for youth development.

“Sports remains an important platform for physical development, talent discovery, unity and the exploration of career opportunities for young people. The Sports Fiesta was designed to go beyond sporting competitions by providing students with opportunities to discover their talents and develop their potential,” Ananaba said.

On his part, the Founder and Pro-Chancellor of Lux Mundi University, Umuahia, Professor Gabriel Okenwa, who spoke on behalf of private universities, commended Otti for his transformational leadership.

“Good governance deserves commendation irrespective of political affiliation. Governor Otti has shown visionary and transformational leadership, particularly in infrastructure, education and human capital development,” Prof. Okenwa said.

In his opening address, the Chairman of the Central Organising Committee and Special Adviser to the Governor on Tertiary Education, Dr. Emeka Enyiazu, said the fiesta breaks institutional barriers.

“The fiesta has provided a common platform for federal, state and private tertiary institutions, including universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, to showcase their sporting talents. It is an opportunity to break institutional barriers, discover hidden talents and prepare young athletes for national and international competitions,” Enyiazu said.

He urged athletes to compete with courage and uphold fair play.

In her vote of thanks, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Tertiary Education, Mrs. Chinyere Okeziem-Nwoko, appreciated Otti for his commitment to educational advancement and youth empowerment.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Highlights of the ceremony included the official unveiling of the New Abia Crusaders Club, administration of oaths to athletes and officials, and a parade by representatives of various tertiary institutions.

The 2026 Abia State Tertiary Education Sports Fiesta was organised by the Ministries of Tertiary Education and Youth and Sports Development.

title: I’m getting back to my best, says Man City’s Foden
excerpt: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is getting back to his PFA and Premier League Player of the Season form ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match at RB Leipzig.
description: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is getting back to his PFA and Premier League Player of the Season form ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match at RB Leipzig.
content:
Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is getting back to his PFA and Premier League Player of the Season form ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match at RB Leipzig.

Foden won the Premier League and PFA Player of the Season awards in 2024 after scoring a career-best 27 goals in all competitions.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Speaking in Leipzig on Tuesday, Foden said he felt he was getting back to his best after a disappointing run of form which led to him missing selection for the 2026 World Cup.

Foden scored a hat-trick and laid on an assist as City beat AEK Athens in their most recent Champions League match in October.

“Consistency, just keep playing regularly, being happy, positive and being in the right positions to score as well,” Foden said of the ingredients needed to return to form.

“So hopefully I can get back to that level. I think I’m slightly starting to get back there now in my recent performances.

“So I hope they just keep going and keep getting back.”

“Being involved in goals gives you a lot of confidence, and when you’re playing regularly as well, you kind of just get into a rhythm and a groove.”

Foden said he had not spoken to England manager Thomas Tuchel since being left out of the World Cup squad.

“All I try and do really is focus on my own game, and hopefully one day the call-up might come back soon,” Foden said.

The 26-year-old local junior grew up a Manchester City fan but declined to comment on the impact of the Premier League’s charges against the club for breaching financial regulations.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Respectfully, I’d just like to talk about the game and not answer anything like that.”

Foden said he felt the transition from long-time City manager Pep Guardiola to new coach Enzo Maresca, who joined in the summer, was easier for him as he had worked under the Italian at youth level.

“I understand him more than the other players because I’ve worked with him in the past so that helps me try and help the team.”

Maresca agreed that Foden was improving and backed him to have an impact this season, although he acknowledged that the attacking midfielder was competing for a place with Rayan Cherki.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“I see Phil day by day better and better, for sure, 100 per cent. He’s going to give us many things this season.

“I said many times that Phil and Rayan are more or less in the same position, but again, I’m very, very happy with the way Phil is working every day.”

content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi State.

The operation took place on Tuesday in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela-Odolu Local Government Area, as troops continued efforts to track fleeing suspects following a raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the same forest on Monday.

---

Abdullahi said troops sustained their operations in the forest to locate fleeing suspects, clear remaining hideouts and restrict the movement of criminal elements.

He said the troops made contact with the suspects during the follow-up operation and engaged them, forcing them to retreat.

“The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of two kidnappers, while others fled into the surrounding forest,” he said.

A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, 438 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition and 4,725 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Other items recovered included two bandoliers, two mobile phones and a power bank.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that troops had dismantled a suspected kidnappers’ camp in the forest during Monday’s operation, recovering about 1,000 rounds of ammunition and six motorcycles.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Abdullahi said Tuesday’s operation had consolidated the gains of the earlier raid, adding that troops remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal groups.

He said the brigade would continue operations to protect lives and property and support efforts to restore lasting peace across Kogi State.

The National Sports Commission (NSC) disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Head of Press and Public Relations, Zira Zakka Nagga.

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

According to the commission, each player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while each coach and official received the equivalent of $50,000.

The Chairman of the NSC, Shehu Dikko, thanked Tinubu for fulfilling his pledge, saying the President had directed that all aspects of the reward package be delivered within a reasonable time.

“The Super Falcons made Nigeria proud, and Mr President has honoured his commitment to them in full. This means a great deal to the team and to Nigerian sports,” Dikko said.

He said the President’s action marked a departure from previous experiences in which some Nigerian athletes waited years to receive promised rewards.

“Some of our sports heroes endured years of waiting for promises to be fulfilled. President Tinubu has shown that things can be done differently,” he said.

Dikko added that the fulfilment of the pledge would encourage athletes to represent the country with confidence that their efforts would be recognised.

He also said the gesture would inspire young Nigerians, particularly girls aspiring to pursue careers in sports.

The NSC chairman recalled that Nigeria’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress, received similar cash rewards in September 2026 after winning their fifth consecutive FIBA Women’s AfroBasket title in 2025.

Each D’Tigress player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while officials received $50,000 each. The team had also received three-bedroom apartments and national honours.

Dikko also cited the completion of rewards for the Super Eagles following their silver-medal finish at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations, held in Côte d’Ivoire in 2024.

He thanked the Ministers of Finance, Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, and Housing and Urban Development for their roles in completing the reward package.

“Delivering these rewards required close cooperation across government. We appreciate the Honourable Ministers and their teams for working with the Commission to complete the necessary processes,” he said.



---

The commission congratulated the Super Falcons’ players, coaches and officials on their achievement, urging Nigerian athletes preparing for future competitions to draw encouragement from the fulfilment of the President’s promises.

title: Ogun govt, Ijebu Chiefs clash over Awujale Council as succession crisis deepens
excerpt: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing
description: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing
content:
…State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

A fresh controversy has erupted over the administration of Ijebuland following the decision of the Ogun State government to reconstitute the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), barely a day after traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode announced the dissolution of the council and its replacement with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.

The development has exposed a disagreement between the state government and some traditional authorities over the appropriate legal and customary structure for administering Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale.

While the government insists that the AIAC remains the only legally recognised administrative body authorised to oversee the affairs of Ijebuland during the interregnum, the traditional chiefs maintain that the Adele Oba Awujale in Council is rooted in the customs and established traditional practices of the Ijebu people.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat, the state government said the withdrawal of some members of the AIAC did not invalidate the council or confer legal authority on another body to take over its responsibilities.

The government described the AIAC, established in August 2025, as the only legally recognised administrative structure empowered to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland until a new Awujale is appointed and crowned.

It specifically clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal from the council.

Dismissing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, the government maintained that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy laws of Ogun State.

According to Hamzat, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the administration of the vacant Awujale stool.

The government also faulted the reliance on the Chiefs Law of 1957 by some former members to justify the emergence of the new body, arguing that the legislation was enacted before Nigeria’s independence and no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976.

To support its position, the state government cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others.

It said the judgment affirmed the legality, validity and authority of the AIAC as the administrative body established by the government to oversee the affairs of Ijebu-Ode pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale.

The government noted that all members of the council were parties to the suit and had consented to the judgment.

It further stated that the court had affirmed that where there was a conflict between the administrative responsibilities of the AIAC and the traditional functions of the Olisa, the authority of the administrative body would take precedence.

The statement added that the judgment had not been appealed and remained binding on the parties.

Although acknowledging the right of individual members to withdraw from the council, the government warned that such a decision could not confer legal authority on another group to assume the functions of the AIAC.

It consequently cautioned members of the public against conducting official transactions or administrative dealings with individuals who had withdrawn from the council in their purported capacity as members of an alternative administrative body.

The government also urged the former members to refrain from actions capable of violating the law or threatening peace and stability in Ijebuland.

Consequently, it announced the reconstitution of the AIAC to ensure continuity in the administration of the ancient town.

The reconstituted council comprises Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, as Chairman; Chief Chris Okunowo, Bobasuwa, as Secretary; Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso; Chief Stephen O. Bakare, Babalaje; and Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun, as members.

The government said the council would continue to discharge its legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned.

……..Chiefs insist on traditional authority

However, the government’s position came against the backdrop of a resolution adopted on Monday by traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode to dissolve the AIAC and replace it with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.

The resolution was reached at a meeting involving the Ilamuren, Pampa, the Odi and other traditional chiefs of Ijebu-Ode, where the leaders reportedly agreed that members of the existing AIAC should step down from their positions and assume membership of the newly constituted body.

The state government had established the AIAC in August 2025, about a month after the death of the 91-year-old Awujale, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland during the transition period.

The initial administrative arrangement was chaired by Chief Folorunso Kuku, the Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland and co-founder of EKO Hospital, Lagos, who is also designated as one of the Ilamuren.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

But in a resolution signed by the Chairman of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, Olo’rgun Dr Sonny Kuku, the traditional chiefs said their decision to replace the AIAC was informed by their interpretation of the existing traditional and statutory frameworks governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution.

They argued that the Ogun State Chiefs Law 2021 did not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council or prescribe a general procedure for appointing a regent during an interregnum.

The chiefs, however, maintained that the Chiefs Law and the 1957 Declaration provided a framework for recognising customary arrangements, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.

The resolution stated: “Upon consideration of the applicable traditional and statutory framework, it was observed that the Ogun State Chiefs Law of 2021 does not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council, nor does it prescribe a general procedure for the appointment of a Regent.”

It added: “It was further noted that the Chiefs Law and Declaration of 1957 provide an existing framework within which customary declarations are made and recognised, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.”

Explaining the decision to replace the AIAC, the chiefs said: “In view of the foregoing, a motion was moved and unanimously adopted that all members of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC) should formally step down from their existing positions and transition into the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.”

They further declared that the new body would assume responsibility for the administration of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum.

“Consequently, the Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth assume responsibility for the administration of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum and exercise, on an interim basis, such administrative powers and functions as may appropriately be required in the absence of the Awujale, subject to applicable laws and established customs and traditions,” the resolution stated.

The 14-member Adele Oba Awujale in Council comprises Dr Sonny Kuku, who holds the Ogbeni Oja title; Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Olisa; Chief O.B. Okuboyejo, Obasewa; Chief Chris Funmilola Okunowo, Bobasuwa; and Chief Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso.

Other members are Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Olootu Olowa; Chief Jimi Lawal, Olotu Ifore; Chief Kunle Ogunade, Apebi; Chief Mrs B.O. Osibogun, Iyalode; Chief Adegoke Balogun, Jaginrin; Chief Agboola Alausa, Balogun; Chief Abimbola Okenla, Kakanfo; Chief Adebisi Adaran, Ogbeni Odi Awujale; and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja, Lapoekun.

The traditional leaders described the arrangement as a recognised customary administrative structure designed to ensure continuity and stability in Ijebu-Ode while the process of selecting and installing a substantive Awujale continues.

“The Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth serve as the recognised traditional administrative body for the management of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode throughout the interregnum, in accordance with applicable laws, customary practices and the established traditions of Ijebuland,” the statement declared.

The chiefs also maintained that their decision was anchored on the customs and longstanding cultural practices of the Ijebu people, particularly those governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“Our position is firmly rooted in the ancient customs, established cultural practices and time-honoured traditions of the Ijebu people, particularly as they relate to the Awujale Chieftaincy Institution,” they stated.

They added that the resolution was intended to protect the integrity of the traditional institution and preserve the historical framework of Ijebuland until a new Awujale emerges.

title: Olodo murder: Police arrest two suspects, deploy Army, Amotekun

content:
.as tension grips Ibadan community

The Oyo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the killing of a 26-year-old man, identified as Kehinde Asimiyu, following a fatal altercation at Olodo Garage in the Lagelu Local Government Area of Ibadan, while reinforcing security in the area to prevent a breakdown of law and order.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The development came amid heightened tension in the Olodo community following the fatal stabbing of the young man, popularly known as KBlaq, by a commercial motorcyclist during a disagreement over transport fare, an incident that disrupted commercial activities and forced residents and commuters to trek considerable distances after motorcycle operators withdrew their services over fears of possible reprisal attacks.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said the command received a report of the incident on 1 November 2026, indicating that the deceased had allegedly been stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde following an altercation between the two men at Olodo Garage.

According to the police, “the deceased was allegedly stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde at Olodo Garage following an altercation between both parties.”

The statement added that the incident subsequently came to the attention of the deceased’s family when “an unidentified motorcycle rider arrived at their residence and informed them of the attack.”

“Following receipt of the report, police operatives, accompanied by a patrol team, immediately mobilised to the scene, while the victim was rushed to Academy Hospital, Texaco, Iwo Road, Ibadan, where he was confirmed dead by the doctor on duty.“

“His remains were subsequently deposited at Adejare Embalming Centre for preservation, while photographs were taken as part of the preliminary investigative procedures.“

The police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the killing had led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as Taiwo Babarinde, suspected to have inflicted the fatal injury on the deceased, and Ishola Semiu, suspected of involvement in the incident.

“Both suspects are currently in Police custody, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for comprehensive investigation,” the statement said.

However, the police intervention following the killing also witnessed a fresh security challenge, as unrest reportedly erupted at the Olodo Police Outpost, nearly resulting in a breakdown of law and order.

The situation was further compounded by subsequent reports of threats from hoodlums, prompting the immediate reinforcement of security across the area to prevent further disturbances and protect residents.

Consequently, the Commissioner of Police, CP Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, directed the deployment of additional operational assets, with personnel of the Nigerian Army, Amotekun Corps, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other local law enforcement components joining the security operation.

The command said the coordinated deployment had helped restore normalcy, adding that there was now a sustained security presence in the area “to forestall further disturbances and protect residents.”

In a further move to address the underlying tensions, the Commissioner of Police directed the Area Commander, Moniya, to engage relevant community stakeholders towards addressing the situation and preventing a recurrence.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Acting on the directive, the Area Commander earlier on Tuesday held a strategic meeting with representatives of the Local Council Development Area (LCDA), leaders of tricycle and motorcycle operators, as well as youth leaders.

The engagement, according to the police, “focused on identifying practical solutions, strengthening communication with security agencies and promoting peaceful coexistence among residents and other stakeholders.”

Reassuring residents of the command’s commitment to their safety, the police said: “The Command reassures residents of Olodo and its environs that adequate security measures remain in place to safeguard lives and property.”

The command also issued a stern warning to those seeking to exploit the situation to foment trouble, incite violence or destabilise the area.

“It also issues a stern warning to individuals or groups seeking to foment trouble, incite violence or exploit the situation to destabilise the area that such conduct will not be tolerated,” the statement added.

It further declared that: “The Command will decisively deal with anyone whose actions threaten public peace or undermine the security gains recorded across Oyo State.”

The Commissioner of Police also appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating the crisis.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He urged them to “remain calm, shun violence and embrace dialogue as a means of resolving disagreements.”

He further encouraged community members to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information, while reiterating the command’s determination to sustain the prevailing peace and ensure the safety and security of all residents.

title: APC rejects Tinubu campaign council list in Osun, demands review
excerpt: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun has rejected its State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) list, alleging breaches of party guidelines and exclusion of key officials.
description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun has rejected its State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) list, alleging breaches of party guidelines and exclusion of key officials.
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun has rejected its State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) list, alleging breaches of party guidelines and exclusion of key officials.

Mr Wole Adunola, Osun APC Publicity Secretary, disclosed this in a statement jointly signed by two other party officials on Tuesday in Abuja.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Adunola said the list failed to reflect due process, inclusiveness and respect for established party structures.

He said the exclusion of several State Working Committee members, who should be statutory members, informed the rejection.

“Of particular concern is the omission of several members of the State Working Committee who, according to applicable guidelines, are expected to be statutory members of the council,” he said.

Adunola said the exclusion raised concerns about consultation, due process and respect for the party’s established leadership structure.

He also questioned the composition of the council in relation to an earlier presidential directive reportedly naming Gov. Ademola Adeleke as its Director-General.

According to him, Adeleke subsequently inaugurated a broad-based campaign team to coordinate President Bola Tinubu’s presidential campaign across the state.

Adunola said it was unclear why a different structure had emerged without adequate clarification or alignment with the existing arrangement.

He suggested that the newly released list might have been intended for a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the PCC.

“If the newly released list was intended to serve as a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the PCC, its composition would be more understandable,” he said.

Adunola said the distinction must be clarified to prevent confusion, duplication of responsibilities and unnecessary friction within the party’s campaign structure.

He stressed that the State Executive Committee remained integral to the APC’s organisational framework and should not be sidelined.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“A successful campaign must be built on mutual respect, proper coordination, and the active involvement of legitimate party stakeholders,” he said.

Adunola called for an immediate review of the list, with consultations involving relevant stakeholders, including APC National Secretary, Sen. Surajudeen Basiru, and the State Director-General.

He said the consultations would ensure proper alignment, effective coordination and respect for established party procedures.

Adunola reaffirmed the chapter’s commitment to Tinubu’s re-election bid and the overall interests of the APC.

He, however, warned that party loyalty should not prevent constructive engagement when decisions risk creating avoidable divisions and undermining collective efforts.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He urged party leaders at state and national levels to address the concerns promptly and make the necessary corrections.

Adunola said an effective campaign council must accommodate legitimate stakeholders, recognise established leadership and unite members towards electoral victory.

title: EFCC Links Illegal Mining To Insecurity, Organised Crime, Vows To Target Financiers
excerpt: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has linked illegal mining and the theft of mineral resources to rising insecurity and organised crime in Nigeria, warning tha...
description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has linked illegal mining and the theft of mineral resources to rising insecurity and organised crime in Nigeria, warning tha...
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has linked illegal mining and the theft of mineral resources to rising insecurity and organised crime in Nigeria, warning that criminal networks are exploiting weaknesses in the mining sector to fund other criminal activities.

EFCC Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, said efforts to tackle illegal mining must go beyond arresting miners at illegal sites to dismantling the networks of financiers, mineral buyers, compromised public officials and other beneficiaries behind the operations.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He spoke while delivering a keynote address at a public lecture and capacity-building workshop organised by the Michael Imoudu National Institute for Labour Studies in collaboration with the Human and Environmental Development Agenda in Ilorin, Kwara State, on Tuesday.

“There is a close connection between resource theft and insecurity. From an enforcement perspective, any economic activity that operates substantially outside regulation creates opportunities for criminal interests,” Olukoyede said.

He explained that illegal mining creates opportunities for extortion, smuggling, violence and territorial disputes, while proceeds from the activities could also finance other forms of criminality.

“They can include extortion, smuggling, violence, competition over territory and the financing of other forms of criminality. This is why we must stop looking at illegal mining only as a licensing problem,” he added.

The EFCC chairman disclosed that the commission recorded 52 illegal mining cases between October 2023 and July 2026 and secured the forfeiture of 102 tonnes of solid minerals through its enforcement activities.

According to him, investigations have exposed sophisticated networks involving local and international players, with different individuals responsible for financing operations, extracting minerals, arranging transportation, facilitating documentation and purchasing illegally obtained resources.

He said the commission’s strategy was to follow the financial transactions behind illegal mining and identify those benefiting from the proceeds.

“Therefore, dealing with illegal mining involves breaking an impregnable chain of fraudulent actors: young men carrying shovels, their financiers, buyers of the minerals, compromised officials facilitating the operation, beneficiaries from the proceeds and other actors.

“A serious enforcement strategy must move from the pit to the purse,” Olukoyede emphasised.

The EFCC boss clarified that the commission was not responsible for regulating the mining sector or issuing mining licences, explaining that its intervention focused on suspected corruption, fraud, money laundering, illicit financial flows and criminal proceeds.

He said financial investigations were critical because proceeds from illegally extracted minerals eventually entered the financial system through payments, bank accounts, business transactions and asset acquisitions.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Olukoyede also warned that public officials who abused their positions to facilitate illegal mining, manipulate licences or launder proceeds from mineral theft would not be spared.

On inter-agency cooperation, the commission’s chairman called for stronger collaboration among mining regulators, financial intelligence institutions, law enforcement agencies, customs authorities and revenue agencies to improve intelligence sharing and coordinate investigations.

He identified fragmented information among government institutions as one of the challenges confronting efforts to track criminal networks.

Olukoyede urged agencies to coordinate investigations across the entire mining value chain, from licence ownership and mineral extraction to buyers, financial transactions and ultimate beneficiaries.

He also called on host communities, traditional institutions, civil society organisations and local leaders to report suspicious mining activities, while urging organised labour to demand lawful mining practices and decent working conditions.

The EFCC chairman reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to investigating financiers and facilitators, tracing illicit proceeds, recovering criminal assets and prosecuting suspects based on evidence.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He maintained that Nigeria’s mineral resources should translate into economic prosperity for citizens rather than serve as a source of wealth for criminal networks.

title: Security Operatives Rescue Eight Kidnap Victims In Kaduna
excerpt: Security operatives have rescued eight persons abducted by suspected kidnappers in Millennium City and Maraban Rido communities of Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State.
description: Security operatives have rescued eight persons abducted by suspected kidnappers in Millennium City and Maraban Rido communities of Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State.
content:
Security operatives have rescued eight persons abducted by suspected kidnappers in Millennium City and Maraban Rido communities of Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State.

The victims were rescued between October 31 and November 2, 2026, during coordinated operations involving the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Police Force and the military, in collaboration with the Kaduna State Government.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Addressing a press conference at the DSS Command Headquarters in Kaduna on Tuesday, the state Commissioner of Police, Muhammad Rabiu, said the operations were part of sustained efforts to identify, disrupt and dismantle criminal networks responsible for recurring abductions in Millennium City and neighbouring communities.

He said the persistent kidnapping incidents in the area had generated considerable public concern over the safety of residents and other stakeholders.

The rescued victims were identified as Jamila Muhammad, Talatu Yakubu, Yunana Bawa, Calista Bishop, Chidinma Onuwere, Eucharia Obi, Godiya Victor and Miracle Alex, an eight-year-old girl.

The latest rescue came barely weeks after security agencies freed Ahmad Zakka and members of his family from captivity on October 15, 2026.

Rabiu described the successive operations as evidence of the determination of security agencies to secure the release of abducted persons and dismantle criminal networks operating across Kaduna State.

He acknowledged the strategic coordination provided by the Office of the National Security Adviser, the operational support of the police, the intelligence-driven efforts of the DSS and the involvement of the military.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The police commissioner also commended the Kaduna State Government under Governor Uba Sani for its continued support and cooperation with security agencies in tackling kidnapping and banditry across the state.

He further disclosed that additional personnel and security equipment, including 30 patrol vans and eight armoured personnel carriers, would be deployed to strengthen operations and improve security coverage in vulnerable areas.

Identifying the difficult terrain in parts of Kaduna State as one of the challenges exploited by criminal elements, Rabiu assured residents that ongoing operations would be sustained and strengthened to deny kidnappers and bandits freedom of action.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He urged residents to complement the efforts of security agencies by remaining vigilant and providing credible, timely and actionable intelligence on the identities, activities and movements of suspected kidnappers and other criminal elements.

description: Reporters, photographers and video journalists are deployed by AFP across the United States to document the 2026 midterm elections as Americans head to the polls.
content:
Reporters, photographers and video journalists are deployed by AFP across the United States to document the 2026 midterm elections as Americans head to the polls.

Here is a round-up of interviews on Tuesday at polling stations where voters agreed to share their thoughts about what was on their minds and motivating their choices.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

With polling data suggesting the Democratic Party is on track to capture a majority in the House of Representatives and perhaps even in the Senate, many left-leaning voters said they were hopeful about the results.

“Two years ago was a really devastating outcome for me,” Emma Mondadori, a 39-year-old who works in philanthropy, told AFP in Brooklyn, New York, referring to President Donald Trump’s election.

“I’ve been really looking forward to this day where we get to have a say again in the future of our country… I’m cautiously hopeful, optimistic.”

With gasoline prices up by a third since last year and diesel nearly double — not to mention sharp food price inflation — everyday spending was on many people’s minds.

“It’s about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things. It needs to change for the everyday person, and I’m an everyday person,” Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in Atlanta, Georgia, told AFP.

Tom, a 27-year-old businessman at the same polling station who declined to give his surname, agreed.

“Everyone, at least in my generation, is a little frustrated with the affordability crisis and gas prices and what’s going on abroad,” added the non-partisan voter.

Mid-term elections are typically seen as a form of referendum on the sitting president.

And few leaders have polarized public opinion as strongly as Donald Trump.

“I’m independent but I voted Democrat, I just wanted to go back into the culture of decency, integrity, honesty, and the rest follows,” Yan Cardineau, 59, told AFP in Austin, Texas. “If we lose that, it doesn’t matter how much money you make.”

Estrella Roque, a 69-year-old voter of Cuban origin, told AFP in Miami she had voted Republican.

“What I like about the Republicans is that they can fix the country,” she explained in Spanish. “Donald Trump hasn’t been given time to show who he really is.”

In his final pitch to voters, Trump has stressed his success in reducing immigration and stopping crossings along the southern border with Mexico.

While his tough stance plays well with his core supporters, others have been put off by the brutal tactics used by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.

“I am very concerned about climate change, school violence and the situation with people who still don’t have immigration status in this country,” Diana Alvarez, a 38-year-old Cuban-born attorney said in Doral, Florida.

“It’s tough for any presidency, but this one in particular has been a little violent and aggressive (with migrants) and I don’t think that was necessary.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Trump’s most consequential foreign policy decision of his second term  — the February 28 attack on Iran along with Israel  —  was referenced by several voters.

“It’s discouraging. Again, promises made, promises not kept. ‘No new wars’ was the mantra,” Wes Pyron, a 37-year-old who works at an environmental health nonprofit in Washington, said.

“I don’t understand what we’re doing there, objectives aren’t clear, priorities aren’t clear.”

Many Republican candidates and Trump have sought to portray their Democratic rivals as dangerous tax-and-spend Socialists intent on destroying American capitalism.

“A lot of today’s younger people think socialism is the way to go,” Daryl Ruley, an 84-year-old in Austin, Texas, told AFP. “They don’t understand history if they believe that’s the case.”

Maru Restrepo, a 70-year-old voter of Colombian origin in Miami, said Democrats had become “very Socialist, Communist, and Muslim.”

In one of the most widely watched races for the Senate  — in Michigan  — Democrat candidate Abdul El-Sayed has made free universal healthcare and ending US support for Israel key planks of his platform.

The Muslim former medical administrator has been called a jihadist by Trump and has been smeared with accusations of sympathizing with Islamist groups such as the Muslim Brotherhood or Hamas.

“We just got to get it done because we all need help. I need help,” said Makeyla Borndes, a 51-year-old former teacher who was forced to retire after falling down a staircase.

Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. --- ### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. title: INEC flags 268 records over AI photos, irregularities
excerpt: The Independent National Electoral Commission has flagged 268 records in its preliminary Register of Voters for suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other...
description: The Independent National Electoral Commission has flagged 268 records in its preliminary Register of Voters for suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other...
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has flagged 268 records in its preliminary Register of Voters for suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other irregularities, as it begins a process to clean up the database ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, disclosed this on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics, explaining that the Automated Biometric Identification System had identified the questionable records for further examination.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“What we are currently doing now is looking at all these 268 records that ABIS already flagged as AI-generated or even something of irregularities,” he said.

Bayode explained that some individuals allegedly exploited a special registration option designed for persons with disabilities who have incomplete fingers or no fingers to create questionable voter profiles.

He said the option, known as special registration, was among the loopholes allegedly exploited by those responsible for the irregularities detected by the system.

The ICT director said the commission had commenced the process of removing the affected records from the preliminary register.

“Those that we have seen, we are cleaning up,” Bayode said.

He, however, clarified that photographs enhanced with artificial intelligence would not automatically lead to the exclusion of affected voters, distinguishing between genuine photographs improved with AI applications and images generated entirely by artificial intelligence.

“Those that we know it is the AI on the phone that helped enhance their pictures, we can’t exclude such people because it was the AI on the phone that does that.

“Such people will still be on the register but those AI-generated, those photographs, all these will be removed. We are already looking at them,” he said.

The development followed the publication of INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters on its website on October 26, which triggered public outrage after screenshots circulated on social media showing suspicious photographs attached to voter records, particularly in parts of Edo State.

The controversy also generated concerns over alleged duplicate registrations, the appearance of names of deceased persons and complaints by some registered voters that their details were missing from the online register.

The concerns attracted reactions from political leaders, civil society figures and other Nigerians, who questioned the credibility of the registration process and demanded explanations from the electoral commission.

The Nigeria Democratic Congress vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, called for a thorough, transparent and independent investigation into the alleged irregularities.

Kwankwaso, in a statement shared on his X account, said Nigerians deserved more than assurances from INEC, urging the commission to make the findings of its investigation public and hold anyone found culpable accountable.

“While I welcome INEC’s decision to investigate the matter, but Nigerians deserve more than assurances. The investigation must be thorough, transparent and independent (outside of INEC’s internal affairs), with its findings made public and any individuals found culpable held accountable in accordance with the law,” he said.

He also called for the verification of questionable entries and investigation of possible duplicate or artificial identities to ensure that eligible voters were not disenfranchised.

Similarly, a political economist, Pat Utomi, expressed concern over the development, saying the discovery raised serious questions about the verification and accountability mechanisms of the electoral commission.

In a post on X, Utomi said, “INEC cannot afford to be careless with the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral process. The presence of AI-generated images in a register meant to support our democracy raises serious questions about verification, transparency and accountability. Our democracy is at stake here!”

The National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement, Dr Moses Paul, also demanded explanations from INEC, questioning how the suspected AI-generated photographs found their way into the register.

“OUR DEMOCRACY IS UNDER THREAT! INEC must explain how AI-generated images found their way into a register meant to protect our electoral process. Who verified these records, and who is accountable?” he wrote.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He maintained that Nigerians would not accept silence or secrecy over an issue he said could undermine confidence in democratic institutions.

Also reacting, the Director of the Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre, Clement Nwankwo, questioned the credibility of the voter register, warning that the alleged irregularities could affect the integrity of the 2027 elections.

Speaking during an interview on ARISE News, Nwankwo raised concerns over the increase in the number of registered voters from more than 90 million to 103 million, questioning the accuracy of the figures and the verification procedures.

He said, “Technology has of course come forward, and now what we see is what is now referred to as AI-generated information and photographs that have been inserted into the voter register.”

Nwankwo further argued that the commission needed to improve communication with political parties and provide greater transparency about its preparations for the elections.

He also warned that shortcomings in the voter registration and polling unit transfer processes could lead to the disenfranchisement of eligible voters.

Meanwhile, INEC had earlier defended the publication of the preliminary register, explaining that the online version released on October 26 was the same document physically displayed at Registration Areas nationwide between October 9 and 15.

In a statement issued by the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, the commission said the online publication did not reflect all the data-cleanup activities already underway.

It maintained that the preliminary register was not the final certified document, stressing that the Display, Claims and Objections exercise was designed to enable members of the public to identify inaccuracies, report questionable entries and facilitate corrections before certification.

The commission also said it was investigating the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and would take appropriate action based on verified findings.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

INEC Chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, has also said the commission is examining the records and would take corrective action based on verified findings.

The commission is expected to complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026.

content:
Ebonyi State Government has forwarded an executive bill to the State House of Assembly seeking to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative punishment.

Governor Francis Nwifuru disclosed this at the weekend during the funeral of the slain traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike autonomous community in Ikwo Local Government Area, HRH Eze Francis Igwe.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Igwe, father of the immediate past Deputy Governor of Ebonyi State, Eric Igwe, was abducted on Sunday, March 1, while on his way to church. He was reportedly killed by his abductors a day after.

Speaking at the funeral, conducted by the Assemblies of God Church, Nwifuru lamented what he described as the moral deterioration among Nigerian youths, expressing concern about their readiness to assume leadership positions in the future.

He also pledged to implement any court decision against those arrested over the monarch’s murder, adding that the proposed legislation was intended to deter kidnapping and abduction in the state.

The governor said: “I am worried about our present-day youths taking up leadership positions tomorrow. Some of our youths are not well informed, and they act so irrationally.

“I am concerned because, with some of their attitudinal dispositions, there seems to be no future for our youths.

“The youths need to have a rethink concerning certain actions of theirs, especially as concerns their attitudes towards community leaders. They should desist from treating their leaders as holders of their destinies.”

He warned that the monarch’s murder should be the last such incident in Ikwo and other parts of the state.

“I will not wait to execute the decision of the court over the murderers of this monarch, HRH Eze Francis Igwe. We have sent a bill to the House of Assembly to make kidnapping attract the death sentence by hanging in the state, with no other option. This should serve as a deterrent to those planning a kidnap, whether for political reasons or otherwise,” the governor said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Nwifuru described the late monarch as a forthright, vocal and astute parliamentarian who represented his people effectively in the old Anambra State and attracted development projects to his community, including the popular Folk Technical College, which has produced prominent Nigerians.

In tributes, former governors Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi, as well as former Senate President, Anyim Pius Anyim, described the deceased as a statesman, peacemaker, renowned educationist, administrator and passionate leader who left enduring legacies.They urged the family and the Ikwo people to take solace in his contributions to society.

In his tribute, the monarch’s first son, Igwe, described his father as a devoted family man and role model who guided him on family life, religion, politics and culture.

He said the circumstances surrounding his father’s death remained difficult for the family to comprehend but expressed confidence that his legacies would endure across generations.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Thanking sympathisers and well-wishers who attended the funeral, Igwe disclosed that his father’s last wish was for Governor Nwifuru to secure a second term.

Earlier, in a sermon titled, “Prepare for Eternity”, the General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Nigeria, Rev. Dr. Abel Amadi, represented by the church’s General Treasurer, Rev. Dr. Gabriel Michael, urged Christians to remain prepared for eternity, noting that no one knew the hour of their death.

title: Dangerous spices: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy
excerpt: By Elizabet Adegbesan
description: By Elizabet Adegbesan
content:
By Elizabet Adegbesan

For some years, plantain chip has been one of Nigeria’s ultimate snacks which is affordable, accessible, and portable.But as inflation hovers at historic highs, a sinister economic survival tactic has crept into the informal food sector.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Economy&Lifestyle discovered that to cut costs and keep chips crispy for days, some street entrepreneurs are turning to a dangerous additive: melted cellophane bags.

The mathematics of running a small-scale food business in Nigeria today is brutal.

The price of vegetable oil, cooking gas, and raw plantains has tripled over the last two years.

For vendors like Halima Mohammed, who operates a roadside frying station, the pressure to maintain profit margins without raising prices is suffocating.

“If I increase the price of a small pack from N200 to N400, the students will walk away.

“People don’t have money. So, vendors look for shortcuts to make the oil last longer and keep the chips from getting soggy in humidity.”

The “shortcut” involves tossing polyethylene plastic bags directly into the scalding oil.

As the plastic melts, it blends with the vegetable oil, creating a glazing agent. When the plantain slices are fried in this mixture, they form a glassy, ultra-crisp outer shell.

Crucially for vendors, the plastic coating prevents the chips from absorbing moisture, extending their shelf life from two days to over two weeks.

In the underbelly of Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, the practice is an open secret, driven by sheer desperation.The lifestyle of a micro-entrepreneur in Nigeria is defined by any-way-raw-iron—a slang term for survival by any means necessary.

With no safety nets and a failing grid that forces reliance on expensive petrol generators, the boundary between ethical business and hazardous malpractice has blurred.

Osaro Jimoh, a distributor who supplies packaged chips to traffic vendors on the , admitted that the market rewards the longest-lasting product.

“The boys selling in traffic need chips that stay crunchy under the hot sun for days. “If the chips go soft, the motorists will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch.

“I don’t know the preservative used to achieve such crunchiness.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

For the millions of consumers who rely on these cheap snacks to get through grueling multi-hour commutes, the lifestyle implications are passive but deadly.

Plastic-infused oil releases carcinogenic compounds, heavy metals, and microplastics into the food, posing severe long-term risks to liver and kidney health.

Agencies have repeatedly warned the public against consuming street foods prepared with plastic additives.However, enforcing regulations in a vast, informal economy is nearly impossible.

Millions of fryers operate out of residential backyards, unbranded and untraceable.

“We are looking at a ticking time bomb of gastrointestinal complications and cancer cases,” he warned.“But you cannot solve a public health crisis without addressing the economic reality.

The naira’s exchange rate against the US dollar remains a major focus for businesses, importers, investors and Nigerians who depend on foreign currency for international transactions.

The Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market are two major segments of Nigeria’s foreign exchange market, with rates varying according to currency supply, demand and market conditions.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

As of Monday, November 2, 2026, the latest available figures indicate that the official NFEM rate stood at ₦1,346.26 per dollar, while the parallel market quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,386.36.

Official NFEM exchange rate

Data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the naira traded at an average rate of ₦1,346.2565 per dollar on Friday, October 30, the latest available official trading data ahead of Monday’s session.

The official market also recorded a closing rate of ₦1,346.00 per dollar, reflecting a marginal improvement from the previous trading session.

The NFEM rate is determined by the volume-weighted average of transactions in the official foreign exchange market. It serves as the benchmark for official foreign currency transactions in Nigeria. Central Bank of Nigeria

Dollar to naira black market rate today

In the parallel market, commonly known as the black market, currency dealers quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,380.59 for buying and ₦1,386.36 for selling as of Sunday, November 1.

This means Nigerians seeking to purchase one dollar from parallel market operators would need approximately ₦1,386, although the actual amount may vary depending on the dealer and location.

The parallel market rates are indicative and may change throughout the day in response to foreign exchange demand and supply.

Difference between official and parallel market rates

The difference between the latest official NFEM weighted average of ₦1,346.26 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,386.36 is approximately ₦40.10 per dollar.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The gap reflects differences in foreign exchange supply, demand and pricing across the two markets.

For individuals and businesses purchasing dollars, the parallel market selling rate remains an important consideration, particularly for transactions that cannot be processed through official banking channels.

How much is $100 in naira today?

At the latest available official NFEM rate of ₦1,346.26, $100 is equivalent to approximately ₦134,626.

At the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,386.36, $100 would cost approximately ₦138,636.

These figures are indicative and do not necessarily represent the final rates offered by banks or individual currency dealers.

Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing exchange rates with their banks or licensed Bureau de Change operators before conducting foreign exchange transactions.

title: Binance resumes withdrawals following $6.3 billion breach
excerpt: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced early on Sunday that it would begin allowing withdrawals in a phased process.
description: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced early on Sunday that it would begin allowing withdrawals in a phased process.
content:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced early on Sunday that it would begin allowing withdrawals in a phased process.

The company froze all deposits and withdrawals after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of crypto from Binance wallets. In its latest update, Binance said it has now covered 95% of the stolen assets, and it’s still working to buy the “remaining affected assets,” which are “less liquid in the market and take longer time to source at the required scale.”

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“Our commitment remains unchanged: Binance will bear the financial impact of the stolen funds,” the company added. “These losses will not be passed on to users.”

As for the withdrawal freeze, Binance said it did not make the decision lightly, as it understands “how important reliable access to withdrawals is for our users.” Nonetheless, the company said this was a necessary “precaution while our teams worked to contain the incident loss, assess its impact, restore affected services, and complete security checks.”

Binance will resume supporting withdrawals in phases, depending on network and asset type. As of Sunday morning, the company’s network status page showed a mix of normal, partially suspended, and fully suspended statuses — for example, Bitcoin withdrawals and deposits are still listed as partially suspended, while Ethereum deposits are normal and withdrawals are partially suspended.

The company also said users should expect “temporary delays or longer processing times due to traffic volume.”

“Resuming withdrawals is a major milestone, but our work continues,” Binance said. “We will continue strengthening our safeguards, completing the recovery process, and providing updates as progress continues.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Binance subsequently shared that between 6am and 3:30pm Coordinated Universal Time, it processed $4.6 billion in withdrawals and $1.0 billion in deposits, for a net outflow of $3.6 billion — 2.1% of its total assets under management.

The company also said it will publish a more in-depth incident report when its investigation is complete.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Binance previously blamed North Korea hackers for the breach. On Saturday, the FBI said that a North Korean group known as TraderTraitor was responsible, and that the group was converting the assets primarily into Ethereum, with further laundering likely.

This post has been updated with information about net outflows during the initial withdrawal period.
