Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!

I’ve joked here and on the Equity and Autonocast podcasts that the autonomous vehicle industry feels a lot like 2016, at least in terms of the buzziness surrounding the sector.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

But a recent conversation with Trucks VC partner Puneeth Meruva has me rethinking that comparison. There’s evidence that 2026 is even hotter — at least by certain measures — than those frothy dealmaking days of 2016 and 2017.

Trucks VC, which specializes in early-stage investing, has fielded pitches from 81 new autonomous vehicle startups so far in 2026 — two-thirds more than last year and enough to surpass the boom years of a decade ago.  The VC firm argues in a new blog post that we’re in the midst of a second, even bigger AV wave fueled by technological breakthroughs. Yes, I’m talking about AI.

“For a long time AV companies were trying to go from what was AV 1.0 to AV 2.0, which is kind of this holy grail end-to-end architecture for AVs,” Meruva told me. “And I think the foundation models now provide a technical architecture that makes those end-to-end systems possible.”

These foundational models are particularly good at generalizing across different environments and scenarios, potentially making AVs cheaper and faster to deploy. The arrival of powerful open source models like Nvidia’s Alpamayo and Qwen’s general-purpose vision-language-action models has made it even easier for startups to get off the ground.

The barrier to entry is lower than ever before. Meruva said Trucks is consistently seeing startups deploy within a few months and with less than $1 million raised. (And while Meruva wouldn’t name names, the firm has invested in some of them.)

Of these 81 startups that pitched Trucks VC, I mistakenly assumed most would be applying their AV tech to construction, warehouse, agriculture, and mining. And yes, those were in the mix. But what surprised me was the growing number of startups pitching pure-play robotaxi businesses. And many are positioning themselves as direct competitors to Waymo.

As wild and galaxy brain-thinking as that may sound, Meruva thinks there is room for smaller players.

“In this world, smaller, more niche autonomy companies can compete — maybe they’re not competing with Waymo on a global scale, but maybe they’re competing in specific regions or specific types of routes,” he said.

And Meruva doesn’t see the pace flattening. He expects even more AV startups to pitch the firm next year.

Regular readers of this newsletter know we’ve been closely following Slate Auto — breaking the original story on Jeff Bezos’ investment way back in April 2025. But the company it spun out of is what got our attention this week.

Re:Build, a Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator, raised $2.1 billion to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.

The company, which was co-founded by Amazon’s former commercial CEO Jeff Wilke, has billed itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen.”

Bedrock Robotics raised $600 million in a funding round that values the autonomous vehicle technology startup at $4.1 billion. CapitalG and Emergence Capital co-led the Series C round. New investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Bessemer Venture Partners, and Temasek participated in the round, alongside existing investors 8VC, Georgian, Valor Equity Partners, Xora, Eclipse, Perry Creek Capital, and Nvidia.

DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart for $17 billion. Meanwhile, DoorDash noted in its third-quarter earnings that it has, so far, only received a few hundred orders from AI agents.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

PreScalar, a San Francisco-based startup developing software and testing infrastructure for factories, raised $7 million in seed funding co-led by Dynamo Ventures and BMW i Ventures, with participation from Blue Wire Capital, Uplift Ventures, and Antler. The startup was founded last year by a trio who had stints at Cruise, Google, Rivian, and Waymo.

Elroy Air, a startup developing autonomous heavy-cargo drones for defense, rapid response, and commercial logistics, hired Jeremy Hux as its CFO in preparation for going public.

Ford announced two new EV chargers that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.

GM is embracing hybrids now. Times sure have changed! The U.S. automaker is also trying to move past the driver data-selling controversy from several years ago. GM agreed to a $220 million settlement with 36 states (its settlement with California and the Federal Trade Commission happened earlier) to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.

Kodiak AI will deliver 75 self-driving trucks to freight company DTL Transport starting in 2028. It’s the company’s first binding commercial deal for driverless big rigs that will run on public highways.

Rivian reported its third-quarter earnings, and a few items stood out to us. For one, the new R2 has been successful enough for the company to raise its 2026 delivery guidance by a couple thousands vehicles. Rivian, which had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year, bumped up that floor to 67,000. But here is another potentially lucrative development: The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants. No word yet on whether that means VW will invest even more money into Rivian.

Tesla turns to Turo to boost adoption of Full Self-Driving (Supervised).

Waymo and Toyota have locked in a manufacturing partnership, officially moving them past the “we’re just talking” phase. Toyota will manufacture AV-ready bZ4X vehicles — and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system — at its factory in Japan. The vehicles will be used for robotaxi services in Japan, the U.K., and other international markets. Importantly, the companies hinted that this could eventually lead to a licensing deal in which Waymo AV tech is in personally owned vehicles.



---

Last call for founders, investors, and builders based in and around the Boston area. The Founder Summit — a one-day event in Boston — will be held on November 4. And I will be there! This event is really geared toward startup founders, aspiring founders, and investors. Attendees can expect advice-driven talks from VCs and serial founders, plus lots of chances to network.

title: AI can make tech CEOs’ lives easier. What about everyone else?
excerpt: Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI.
description: Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI.
content:
Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI.

In Mayer’s case, that involved asking an AI tool for help with a school-assigned description of her daughter. For OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, that’s included suggesting that parents create personalized podcasts for their kids’ drive to school and also declaring that he could not imagine parenting without ChatGPT. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has even suggested that it will become increasingly acceptable to meet your social and romantic needs through AI.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

This all led TechCrunch’s Amanda Silberling to wonder if AI executives are simply too out-of-touch to build products for normal people — a crucial question with Anthropic set to go public just as Wall Street begins losing its appetite for heavy AI spending.

On the latest episode of the Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I chatted with Amanda about why industry leaders can sometimes seem so tone deaf. Kirsten wondered if this is more of a marketing problem or a product problem.

Amanda’s answer: “A little bit of both.” She also argued that the tech industry is increasingly pushing a future “where basic human interaction gets more and more optimized out of actually occurring,” adding, “And call me old school, but I think that humans being able to talk to each other is probably a net positive for society.”

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Anthony Ha: There’s a lot of societal skepticism about AI, this feeling that the people running these companies don’t have our best interests at heart, that they’re out of touch. And so, you would just think, “Maybe don’t make statements like that,” because of course, people are going to see them very skeptically.

I think [CEOs] are trying to walk this delicate balance. On the one hand, there’s a tremendous financial incentive for them to make the case that you should use this technology in every aspect of your lives. But when you make that case, it actually [doesn’t paint] a very appealing picture. In some cases, it’s downright dystopian.

Kirsten Korosec: Anthony, if they took your advice, we would have nothing to talk about on this show.

But I will say this: There’s this whole idea of ChatGPT and other AI tools making your life easier when it comes to personal relationships. And in many of these cases, it just seems to overcomplicate what would be, like, observing your child. That might be hard for some people, the people who are building these products, and it doesn’t necessarily relate to everyone else out there in the world. It can just seem so incredibly disconnected when you see these quotes.

To me, it always comes back to — who are they speaking to? Are there people out there who can relate? Maybe there are.

Amanda Silberling: Other use cases we’ve seen people mention are, like, the Bumble CEO Whitney Wolf Heard has made comments about, “Well, what if we had AI concierges, your AI dates the other person’s AI. And then if the AIs have a good date together, then they introduce the people.”

Or in the New York Times article, Marissa Mayer mentioned, “Well, what if my AI could coordinate with my husband’s AI” and stuff like that. And I think that it feels like people are trying to over-optimize out of just having conversations with people.

I’ve already seen that happen in my generation, where I do notice in myself that if I’m ordering takeout, it feels weird to call a place. I’m just so used to, “Well, obviously you can do it online and you don’t have to talk to anyone. And I feel like there’s just going to be more of these things, where basic human interaction gets more and more optimized out of actually occurring. And call me old school, but I think that humans being able to talk to each other is probably a net positive for society.

Sean O’Kane: Yeah, but what’s the ROI, Amanda? How much revenue can you generate off of a conversation that somebody’s having in meatspace?

Amanda: That is the thing, though. Dating is really inefficient. It sucks that you have to go on a bunch of dates with different people. You might waste an evening and be like, “Well, that was a bust.” And so you can see why people are [wondering,] “What if you didn’t have to go on dates? What if your AI could go on dates for you?” But there’s just something not human there.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

And then also, you are outsourcing the decision of who you are going to date to a computer that you are trusting knows you better than yourself, which I don’t think is true.

Kirsten: One thing that I think is worth going back to, and I sort of hinted about this earlier: Who are they talking to? Who is their audience for all these optimizations, in your view? Is it a product problem, or is it a messaging problem? Are they just talking about it in the wrong way, and actually, there’s this really great value in here and it just seems out of touch with reality and humanity, but if they just talked about it differently, it would be better? Or is it actually a product problem, and to your point, that we’re focusing on optimizing sort of the wrong things with AI tools?

Amanda: I think it’s a little bit of both, but I think that the marketing problem comes from when you have these high-up people at these massively valuable companies in a room together, talking about the pain points in their lives, and [they focus on] making dinner reservations, booking flights. Everybody does those things, but I’m not booking flights once a week. I’m not making dinner reservations all the time. And when I do, those aren’t really things that I find to be a particular challenge in my life.

I mean, obviously people find value from things like ChatGPT and Claude, but I think the value that the average person is finding isn’t necessarily like booking a flight for me.

Anthony:  One of the things I’ve also been thinking about is, there are companies like Uber that, when it first launched, it was targeting this tech early adopter set in San Francisco, and I remember being very confident [that] this will never catch on more broadly. This is just for a very narrow audience of young urban millennials who have money to spare on cars, and it works [uniquely] well in San Francisco.

For a lot of things, the tech industry has succeeded by betting that, “People have not caught up with us, but we are the leading edge, and we reflect what the consumer of the future looks like, the family of the future looks like.”

And in this case, it just seems like that bet is not borne out yet — for a variety of reasons, partly because the society that this technology is being promoted into is very different. People are starting to say, “I don’t love the influence that this technology is having in my life. I don’t love that you’re pitching this as something where every experience in my life should be optimized out of. But actually, I want to live my own life. I actually want to parent my own children.”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Amanda: I think that it’s not a coincidence that at the same time we see this over-optimization happening among people in tech, that there’s also a movement of people that are reverting back to wanting to use flip phones, which I’ve talked about on Equity before, or people who are buying CDs because they’re tired of an algorithm telling them what they want to listen to.

And it is just an interesting cultural tension that’s happening, where we haven’t found the balance of what optimization actually helps us and what optimization just makes us feel like we aren’t as human as we want to be.

content:
Readers don’t typically care who owns what media property, we realize, but last year, we became part of a broader portfolio, a move that has come with some decided benefits, including what amounts to a bigger extended family with cool cousins. Now, in addition to our TechCrunch channels in Slack, we can talk with the writers and editors of CIO, Computerworld, and PCWorld, among other outlets. We also find ourselves reading more of their work  and figured you might like it, too.

Here’s a handful of pieces I was just enjoying while watching the Warriors-Clippers game, which, as I type, is a little too close for comfort:

Cate McHugh was crowned winner of The Voice UK on Saturday night

A singer who began her career as a teenager busking on the streets of Cardiff has been crowned winner of The Voice UK.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Cate McHugh, from Llantwit Major in the Vale of Glamorgan, appeared stunned when she heard her name announced on the ITV show, telling viewers "I did it" when asked how she was feeling.

The performer, who has a degenerative sight condition which has left her registered blind, was given a congratulatory hug by her coach Sir Tom Jones on his final appearance on the show after previously announcing he had been "fired".

Speaking after the show, McHugh, 31, said: "I won The Voice! I'm entirely gobsmacked and absolutely haven't fully processed this information just yet."

Footage shared by McHugh on social media showed her laughing and smiling with family and friends screaming in delight as they celebrated her victory at a watch party in Cardiff.

McHugh's prizes include a £50,000 cash prize and a recording contract, with her first ever single, a cover of The Beatles classic Blackbird, now released.

Posting on social media, she said: "From the bottom of my heart I want to say THANK YOU for following my journey, and joining my world! This is where it's going to REALLY get fun!"

It was also a poignant night for Sir Tom as he made his final appearance on the show

In an interview with BBC Radio Wales Breakfast in September, McHugh said being chosen to be on Team Tom at the blind audition on The Voice UK was "absolutely undescribable".

Her rendition of Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars song Die With A Smile prompted Sir Tom to hit the button to turn his chair around after hearing her.

McHugh said she began singing "before I was talking" and started singing lessons aged six, turning professional when she was about 15.

At 22 she was diagnosed with degenerative sight condition Stargardt disease during her second year at music school and is registered blind.

As it affects the centre of her vision, it meant the singer was not sure if anyone had turned around at her audition until she heard Sir Tom's voice, she added.

"I just waited because I didn't know that anything had happened and then Tom Jones started talking," McHugh said.

She said her "fantastic mother" has the same condition and has been an inspiration to her over the years, "working around anything that might be affecting her physically or mentally".

McHugh said when she phoned her parents to tell them she was on Team Tom "there was this massive roar".

Sir Tom performed a duet with Cate McHugh during the final of The Voice UK

McHugh performed a duet of John Denver's Take Me Home, Country Roads during the final.

Some of her family members could be seen celebrating in the audience during the show.

Sir Tom announced his departure from The Voice UK on Instagram in September

The It's Not Unusual and What's New Pussycat? singer made headlines after revealing that ITV had "made the decision" to "fire" him from the show's coaching panel.

title: Russell Brand accusers 'haunted' for years by alleged crimes, court hears

content:
Some of the women in Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault case have been "haunted" for years by what they allege he did to them, jurors have been told.

In her closing speech at London's Southwark Crown Court on Friday, prosecutor Reil Karmy-Jones KC said the women had "nothing to gain" from coming forward apart from "some closure".

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Speaking for the defence, Polly Dyer told jurors Brand had pleaded guilty and been fined over possession of cannabis in 1995, but had no other "convictions, cautions, reprimands or warnings".

Brand, 51, is on trial facing seven charges; three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of attempted indecent assault. He denies the charges.

Karmy-Jones KC told the court that this case brings together six different women, none of whom knows each other.

She said that while all the alleged victims have since moved on with their lives, due to this trial they have been forced to "relive what has happened to them".

None of the women involved has "sought the limelight" or "any kind of publicity", she said, adding there was "no benefit to them from perhaps some closure."

Referring to Brand's accusers' evidence the prosecutor said "how many said he was nice and then there was a like a personality change…

"His eyes changed, he snapped, from charming to frightening to nasty," Karmy-Jones KC said.

She added that the complainant's evidence had been that "he didn't listen when I said no, he didn't stop, he didn't care, pulling pushing… thrusting".

"In the rape cases, he kept on going until he achieved his ultimate aim."

The prosecutor also dismissed the idea that a documentary had caused the women to "re-invent" what actually happened.

"There is no magic force in this documentary", she added.

"What in fact happened was these women have realised they are not alone and have bravely come before you to tell the truth."

She added: "Truth they have lived with, which in some cases has haunted them for years."

She told the jury: "The experience of people raped may be something that looms a little bit larger in your mind rather than the intricacies of the outfit.

"The defendant couldn't really remember anything when he was interviewed, in stark contrast to now when he suddenly seems to remember all sorts of details about the week."

You can follow the trial day by day on the BBC podcast Russell Brand on Trial - available on BBC Sounds, YouTube, iPlayer, or wherever you get your BBC podcasts

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Addressing Brand's presented change in character, Karmy-Jones KC told the court "He may now be a completely different person to the man he was between 1999 and 2009."

She added: "He may well look back and not find some of his jokes funny".

"He may now treat women with kindness and consent".

Brand's wife Laura gave evidence yesterday, when she told the court her husband was a "kind and a wonderful father".

Karmy-Jones KC called her Russell Brand's "undoubtedly lovely wife", who "bravely" gave evidence.

However, she also noted that she was not with him at the time many of the alleged acts are said to have taken place.

"The reality is she wasn't there then, for the first five counts, she wasn't with him, nor was she with him for the final two counts."

"Any contact was, I believe, sparse."



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

In the final set of agreed facts in his trial, the court heard from Dyer about Brand's fine after he "pleaded guilty to one charge of possessing cannabis on 20 April 1995".

"He received a fine. He has no other convictions, cautions, reprimands or warnings", she said.

We've had four weeks of suspense, suspicion and very suspect tactics, as some of Britain's biggest stars engaged in a battle of wits to win the most popular show on TV.

The second series of BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors reached its climax on Friday, with the 21 original contestants having been reduced to seven before the final.

They were then whittled down to two winners - with the faithful duo of comedian Romesh Ranganathan and Heartstopper actor Sebastian "Bash" Croft emerging victorious.

The players successfully banished the remaining traitors - Love Island host Maya Jama and YouTuber King Kenny - in dramatic fashion, and the winning pair shared the £83,000 prize for their charities.

What just happened in Celebrity Traitors final?

As it happened: Relive the Celebrity Traitors final

The finale drew an average audience of 11.2 million live viewers, and that number will rise when catch-up is included. Other recent episodes have been watched by more than 15 million, including catch-up.

Kenny reached the final stage, the endgame, after turning on his fellow traitor Maya at the last round table.

Kenny, Romesh and Bash were joined by singer James Blunt in the climax of the endgame, where the remaining contestants gather around a fire pit to decide whether they think there are any traitors left.

When James and Kenny were tied in a vote for who was a traitor, Bash persuaded Romesh to banish Kenny instead of James - thereby securing victory for team faithful.

"Absolutely devastated. Almost scraped it," Kenny seethed. "I was so close, I smelled the victory."

However, he can take consolation from the fact his performance on the show has established him as a mainstream star.

The final reveal of the Celebrity Traitors

In a further twist, James chose another round of voting and was subsequently evicted himself, leaving Romesh and Bash as the last men standing.

"This might actually be the best day of my life," said 24-year-old Bash through tears of joy.

He, too, can expect a major career boost.

Romesh reflected: "I just really hope my mum's proud. And also my youngest son Charlie, who wanted me to come on the show - dad won. Please show me some respect."

The pair will split their winnings between two refugee charities, the Refugee Council and Choose Love.

Traitors Kenny and Maya fell at the final hurdle

The final six: Maya, James, Kenny, Romesh, Leigh-Anne and Bash

Earlier, actor Michael Sheen was murdered in the first action of Friday's episode. "I am incredibly disappointed," he said. "Gutted that I got so close to the end. It's been absolutely unforgettable."

When it came to the endgame, Little Mix singer Leigh-Anne Pinnock was swiftly banished after Kenny voted to remove her.

"I was thinking me and him had a mutual understanding, and now I feel so stupid," she raged.

"But I'm walking away feeling super proud and like I've really accomplished something here."

James Blunt helped retrieve the final prize money in a mission involving dynamite and helicopters

Meanwhile, James B was left rueing one final mistake in a long but valiant catalogue of misjudgements throughout the series.

The singer, who looked aghast when he was attacked by Romesh during the endgame, was then the only one to choose to banish again when it came to the final three.

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

"I've loved trying to work it out, I've loved getting it wrong so often, I've loved the tiny moments when I've got it right," he said wistfully. "I've loved the game."

James Acaster effectively banished himself in a novel twist in the show

Celebrities who departed earlier in the series included ex-EastEnders actor Ross Kemp, model Jerry Hall, sitcom star Miranda Hart, comedian Joe Lycett, presenter Hannah Fry and former BBC journalist Amol Rajan.

This series is also likely to be remembered for the two contestants who made the unorthodox decision to reveal themselves as traitors, before being summarily dispatched by their fellow players.

First, actor Richard E Grant was so giddy to have received the tap on the shoulder that he blurted out his supposedly secret status in episode two.

Comedian James Acaster, meanwhile, was the most reluctant traitor in the history of The Traitors, and unexpectedly gave himself up when he came under pressure at the round table in Thursday's penultimate episode.

There have been reports, external that filming of the scene was paused and he was checked by welfare staff after he became anxious.

Asked about the reports, a BBC spokesperson said on Friday that the safety and welfare of those taking part was the "highest priority", and "players are closely monitored and supported throughout by production which includes a dedicated and experienced welfare team".

Speculation about the round table being heavily edited was fuelled when eagle-eyed viewers noticed, external a shot of Romesh reacting in shock - apparently to James A's initial confession - which in fact seemed to have come from a later moment, after Romesh had voted for James by writing his name on the blackboard.

In the episode, the sequence where the celebrities all voted for James in light of his admission was shown as a relatively quick and straightforward process, raising a question about what prompted Romesh's shocked look.

Acaster did not take part in Friday's edition of spin-off show Uncloaked, which reunited some of the celebrity contestants following the final.

The comedian's bombshell the previous night did provide the programme with a twist to spark it to life after what some viewers saw as a mid-series lull.

On Thursday, the Hollywood Reporter noted, external that the show had achieved record-breaking ratings - before asking: "Why, then, has much of the consensus on social media been that it's all felt a bit dull?"

Some noted a shortage of true back-stabbing, double-crossing and explosive rows - the things, in other words, that viewers love the most - while the celebrities were more chummy and savvy than previous groups of castle dwellers.

And while there was no shortage of big characters, this season lacked an equivalent to Alan Carr, the hugely popular and apparently hapless comedian who lied and murdered his way to an unlikely victory as a traitor last year.

The drama ramped up in the final, though, and Friday's episode is likely to have been the most watched TV programme of the year.

In some ways, all the players on The Celebrity Traitors can be seen as winners.

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

They all got to appear on a hugely popular TV show, rubbing shoulders with other stars and gaining new fans along the way.

But there are certain celebrities, such as Miranda Hart, King Kenny, Maya Jama and Joanne McNally, who have been tipped by industry experts as getting the biggest career boost after the show.

Sebastian "Bash" Croft - who won the game, alongside Romesh Ranganathan - could also now be in line for greater roles.

We've taken a look at the breakout stars of the series and what might lie ahead for them.

After a spell of ill-health, the show has done wonders for bringing Miranda Hart back into the public eye.

There was that incredible “Little Mix Big Mix” viral dance moment, but Hart also displayed a level of vulnerability which stood out in a show where the stars don't really talk about their personal lives.

When her friend Joe Lycett was banished, her tearful reaction to his exit provided a rare poignant moment.

"Connection and laughter and joy are bigger than this game - and to meet someone and just play and laugh, it's all us humans need, you know?" she said.

When she was murdered, she also demonstrated genuine emotion in her response. "Ultimately, in my little personal story, this has been quite extraordinary," she said.

For culture journalist Natalie Jamieson, Hart's openness and relatability made her the "standout" star from this year's series.

And it could also lead to us seeing more of Hart on the small screen. According to The Sun, external, the BBC is looking to bring back her self-titled sitcom after her stint on Celebrity Traitors led to fresh interest in the show.

The BBC declined to comment on the possible return of Hart’s show.

But she’s not the only one who won hearts by showing real warmth.

The same could be said for Romesh Ranganathan - who, in a departure from his usual cynical, deadpan stand-up persona, seemed really to care about his fellow cast members. Jerry Hall also won viewers over with her charming eccentricity.

And then there’s James Acaster, who showed genuine vulnerability as he struggled to come to terms with being a traitor.

Social media users seemed split after his bombshell confession to being a traitor, with some totally exasperated and others saying they respected him for going out on his own terms.

Either way, he's definitely got the nation talking.

When it comes to celebrities who are most likely to see the biggest career boost, most experts say Kenny is King.

Going into the castle, the 29-year-old was best known to younger fans as a member of the popular British YouTube collective Beta Squad.

But Kenny will have been "the least familiar name to a mainstream audience," says showbiz journalist Nikki Onafuye.

That all changed as he was recruited as a traitor, bringing much-needed energy to the turret - and he made it all the way through to Friday night’s tense final.

Having shown he can hold his own alongside established broadcasters, actors and comedians, big things could now be in store for Kenny.

"He 100% has just been minted as a mainstream star now," said Marina Hyde, on The Rest is Entertainment podcast.

“The next steps could be panel shows, presenting roles, reality competitions or entertainment formats,” adds TV reporter Siobhan Synnot.

Fellow traitor Maya Jama also sailed all the way to the final with her cool-as-a-cucumber persona making her a traitor to be reckoned with.

Despite being banished in dramatic fashion, she could now be in line to receive £1m per deal, according to a report in The Times earlier this week, external.

What Celebrity Traitors has done for Jama is allow her to reveal more of her personality than on Love Island, says Onafuye.

But TV reporter Synnot thinks between the two, Kenny has more to gain because he has introduced himself to millions of new viewers - whereas Jama was already one of Britain's best-known TV presenters before Celebrity Traitors.

"Maya's gain is subtler: she can emerge looking less like the presenter of Love Island and more like a genuinely versatile television star," she says.

Of all the comedians in the castle, Joanne McNally was initially the least well known, says Caroline Frost, TV editor at Radio Times.

But she flourished on the show, lasting right up to Thursday's semi-final.

"And she's taken her own path, ignoring the herd and making her own voting decisions, sometimes chaotically, but always with charm, wit and good humour,” says Frost.

The Irish comedian's podcast was already popular before the show.

But after her stint as the joker of the pack, bigger things could now lie in store for her.

Just a few days ago, it was announced, external that her stand-up tour has been extended into 2027, "due to phenomenal demand".

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

And her agents will be "fielding calls" for her to bring her star power to other shows, adds Frost.

As it happened: Relive the Celebrity Traitors final

Culture journalist Jamieson says some of the other female contestants - such as Sharon Rooney, Leigh-Anne Pinnock and Myha'la - also stood out for showing their wit and wisdom, which could serve them well in the outside world.

Things got a bit awkward in one of the episodes, when Sharon disagreed with some of the cast on a challenge, with some social media users saying she was acting in a "childish" way.

But others argued it was a classic case of women being drowned out by men.

"There's been a subtlety in the smartness of women on display here, alongside the frustration of not always being listened to in the game," says Jamieson.

In the end, it was faithful duo Romesh Ranganathan and Sebastian ‘Bash’ Croft who emerged victorious.

Comedian Ranganathan was already a huge star, but the show has introduced Croft, 24, to a much wider audience.

He’s had previous acting roles in Game of Thrones and Heartstopper, but Traitors allowed him to show his own personality, "which as we've seen has endeared him both to other players and the huge watching audience", says Frost.

He is also building his career as a pop star, and he's had a strong presence on social media during the series, posting videos of his tracks.

His debut EP comes out later in November, perfect timing to capitalise on his Traitors win.

What's clear is that the true victors aren't necessarily the ones who get their hands on the prize pot.

Arguably, what matters most is the amount of screen time you get - and what you do with it.

On that note, spare a thought for those who left the show early, such as Amol Rajan, Julie Hesmondhalgh and Hannah Fry.

But all made an impact in their own way and, as Synnot points out, they get "a nice anecdote" for future interviews.

And what of James Blunt, who stole hearts with his military approach to the challenges and eccentric Top Gun-style outfits - and who came so close to winning the whole show?

Maybe he's the mystery man in contention for the new James B(ond) - although his hapless theories could mean he'll be in line to be the new Johnny English instead.

title: Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
excerpt: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has backed the company's massive spending on AI.
description: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has backed the company's massive spending on AI.
content:
Google CEO Sundar Pichai has backed the company's massive spending on AI.

Google-owner Alphabet lost just over $500bn (£374bn) in value on Thursday after it revealed its own artificial intelligence (AI) summaries were hitting search advertising revenue.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Chief business officer Philipp Schindler said Google's "AI mode", where it answers questions conversationally, was eating into the money it makes from ads which appear next to results to traditional search questions.

Yet, Schindler said he felt "very good about our trajectory" with an AI-focused version of the search engine.

Google's role in answering the world's questions has been challenged by the AI boom, with millions of people using programs such as ChatGPT and Claude instead.

Kim Scott, who formerly led Google's advertising business, told the BBC's Today programme that the company would "rather eat its own lunch than allow someone else to eat their lunch" by having its own AI summaries hit its search revenue.

She said that Google was founded on the idea of making long-term bets on technology – even if they hurt the firm in the short term.

"I think they're making a long-term bet on AI," she said.

In its results published on Wednesday, Alphabet revealed that total revenue grew 25% in the three months to the end of September, compared to the same period last year, hitting $127.6bn.

However, the firm did not make as much money as analysts had predicted, particularly in its advertising arm, which spooked many investors.

Shares in the company plummeted over 12% to a six-month low following the release of the results.

By the end of Thursday,  the company's total stock market value had fallen to $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion the day before.

Tracy Woo, a principal analyst at Forrester, said Alphabet's disappointing Search business results "highlights the challenge of funding massive AI investments while maintaining the strength of established businesses."

Microsoft and Amazon also issued updates this week, and joined Google in plans to keep spending huge sums of cash in the ongoing AI race.

But investors appeared dismayed at the impacts these plans are having on the ability of each to keep growing their core lines of business.

Amazon's stock took a hit on Thursday , with its shares falling 6% in after-hours  trading.

Alongside quarterly sales growth of 11%, hitting $201bn, the company shared a staggering cash flow figure of negative $42bn.

That number shows that Amazon is not only spending more money than it makes, but that spending has increased six-fold over the span of three months.

Chief executive Andy Jassy claimed the business was spending in part because it had the chance at, not one, but two businesses that could end up bringing in $1 trillion for Amazon the future.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Jassy noted that Amazon's cloud services business, as well as retail stores, may be those businesses. During a call with financial analysts he also repeatedly mentioned the financial opportunity presented by Amazon making and selling its own computer chips, as well as its AI developer platform Bedrock, which offers paying users access to most major AI models and tools.

"One of the lessons we've learned over 20-plus years is that there is not one tool to rule the world," Jassy said. "People always assume whatever is in the lead early on will be the only thing that people use - it's never true."

As Jassy was asked several times to explain the company's spending, he admitted it "would be more convenient" if it were spread over the next 25 years. "That's not the world we live in," he added.

"We can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size, the revenue, the free cash flow of Amazon."

Wall Street's reaction to Microsoft's update was more muted, with shares falling by less than 1% on Thursday.

The company, which is also one of OpenAI's largest investors, spent around $5bn less on investments dedicated to AI. It also revealed earlier this week plans to cut thousands of workers, which will further reduce the company's costs.

Meanwhile, its revenue grew 19% from a year earlier, hitting $92.3bn for the quarter. Its crucial cloud business grew by 30% to $63bn.

Chief executive Satya Nadella said the use of Copilot, Microsoft's AI chatbot and tool, has seen "automated tasks nearly double since July" as daily users grew by 500% from a year ago.

Usually lower spending and growing sales earns a positive reaction from investors.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

But Woo said Wall Street is trying to look farther into the future when it comes to which businesses will truly make good on their big promises around AI.

"Microsoft's results reinforce that enterprise demand for AI remains strong, but they also highlight a much bigger question facing the technology industry, where AI value will ultimately be captured," Woo said.

content:
Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).

Shares in Intel plummeted by 28% on Friday, while Google owner Alphabet saw its stock price continue to fall another 1.4% after a 12% plunge on Thursday.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025.

While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.

Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800bn between them in 2026.

Alphabet's stock market value fell sharply on Thursday, taking more than $500bn (£374bn) off its market value after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.

At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI.

The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere however, with Intel shedding more than $130bn in value.

The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors.

On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.

In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

Amazon on Thursday revealed it had also spent more cash than it was making, and that spending had increased six-fold over the span of three months.

The company has committed to spending $220bn this year, putting the money towards investments such as AI data centres, network equipment, and servers.

Amazon shares recovered some overnight losses, but were still down by 1.4% at the end of Friday trading.

Reddit stock plunged by 29%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.

Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by 18%, as its daily active user numbers dropped.

Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI.

Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google.

He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out".

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

"The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down."

Many analysts have been debating the possibility of an AI bubble in the stock market.

The worry is that some tech firms will not be able to justify their sky-high valuations because the cost of building AI data centres and developing the software will end up being greater than the money they can make from it.

Kathleen Brookes, research director at trading firm XTB, said there have been many ups and downs in AI trade in recent months.

"Investors have turned ruthless, punishing any signs of disappointment in [third quarter] earnings," she said.

"The AI trade has had a good run in recent years, but now investors want payback, and companies like Alphabet and Intel are in the crosshairs."

However, stock market values for many of these companies remain well above where they were a year ago.

While the Nasdaq closed 2.8% lower, it is up 7.8% over the last year. Similarly Amazon is up nearly 8% over the past 12 months, while Alphabet is down 1.3%.

Brookes noted that November is typically a strong month for stocks.



---

title: NANS National Ex-Officio II, Patience Okoroafo, Raises Alarm Over Alleged Marginalization in Akwa Ibom, Calls for Intervention
excerpt: The Akwa Ibom representative at the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) National Executive Council, Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo, has raised concerns over what she describes as sustained marginalization, exclusion and undermining of her office in the state.
description: The Akwa Ibom representative at the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) National Executive Council, Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo, has raised concerns over what she describes as sustained marginalization, exclusion and undermining of her office in the state.
content:
In a report made public, Okoroafo, who serves as National Ex-Officio II at the NANS National Headquarters, accused the Office of the Special Assistant to the Akwa Ibom State Governor on Students Affairs, Comr. Wisdom Emmanuel, of repeatedly sidelining her despite her position as the state's representative at the national student leadership level.

### Dispute Over Representation and Recognition

According to Okoroafo, she emerged as National Ex-Officio II during the last NANS National Convention, becoming the only Akwa Ibom representative occupying a position at the organisation's National Executive Council.

She maintained that her office carries the responsibility of representing and projecting the interests of Akwa Ibom students within the national student leadership structure.

However, she alleged that since her emergence, her office has not received the recognition and institutional support it deserves.

She specifically questioned the repeated involvement of Comr. Dominic Ernest, her Cross River State counterpart, in student-related engagements and activities within Akwa Ibom State, arguing that such responsibilities should ordinarily fall within her representational mandate.

Okoroafo described the situation as an attempt to undermine her position and diminish the relevance of her office.

### Alleges Gender-Based Discrimination and Lack of Support

The NANS official also expressed concerns that her alleged marginalization may be connected to her gender.

Recounting her experience during the NANS National Convention, she alleged that she faced considerable difficulties as a female candidate seeking to represent Akwa Ibom State at the national level.

She further claimed that although the Special Assistant to the Governor on Students Affairs had indicated that government support would be shared between her and Comr. Dominic Ernest, she eventually received no financial assistance from the office.

According to her, this was unlike the experience of some representatives from other states who allegedly received sponsorship and support from their respective state governments.

Despite the challenges, Okoroafo said she financed her campaign through personal sacrifices and contributions from well-wishers, eventually securing victory and bringing national representation to Akwa Ibom State.

She expressed disappointment that, rather than receiving recognition following her emergence, she had continued to experience what she described as exclusion from important student-related engagements.

### Exclusion from Meeting with ARISE with Renewed Hope Leadership

Another major concern raised in the report was her alleged exclusion from a recent meeting involving frontline student leaders and the leadership of ARISE with Renewed Hope.

The meeting reportedly involved Dr. Wisdom Emmanuel, Engr. Uwem Okoko, Hon. Frank Archibong and the Honourable International Coordinator of ARISE with Renewed Hope.

Okoroafo stated that despite being in Akwa Ibom State when the engagement took place, she was neither invited nor informed about the meeting.

She also alleged that she was not briefed on the discussions or outcomes, despite her position within the NANS national leadership structure.

The controversy was further heightened by a social media explanation reportedly given by Comr. Dominic Ernest, who attributed her absence to a national assignment.

However, Okoroafo disputed that explanation, insisting that she was physically present in Akwa Ibom State on the day of the meeting.

She said the discrepancy raises questions about the circumstances surrounding her exclusion and the accuracy of statements made on her behalf.

### Addresses Allegations Concerning Dominic Ernest's Studentship

Meanwhile, Okoroafo also addressed the ongoing controversy surrounding claims circulating online about the studentship status of NANS Vice President, Special Duties, Comr. Dominic Ernest.

She stated that, to the best of her knowledge, Ernest contested the recently concluded NANS National Convention as a student of Cross River State University of Education, Akamkpa.

However, she clarified that determining or declaring his current studentship status was not within her responsibility.

Her position, therefore, was limited to the information available to her regarding his participation in the convention.

### Calls on NANS Leadership and Akwa Ibom Government to Intervene

In her appeal, Okoroafo called on the NANS National Secretariat, the Senate President of NANS, relevant authorities and other stakeholders to intervene and address what she described as the continued marginalization of her office.

She emphasized that her mandate was obtained through the votes of Nigerian students and should be respected irrespective of her gender.

She also appealed for fairness, equity, justice and inclusion within the student leadership structure.

The report was copied to Governor Umo Eno, the NANS National Global President, the NANS Senate President, the Akwa Ibom State Commissioner for Education, security agencies, NANS Zone B leadership and other relevant student leaders.

### The Bigger Question: Representation and Inclusion in Student Leadership

The controversy has brought renewed attention to questions surrounding representation, institutional recognition and inclusion within student leadership structures.

At the centre of the dispute is a fundamental question: Should an elected or conventionally selected representative be excluded from engagements relating to the interests of the constituency they represent?

As the concerns raised by Okoroafo come to public attention, clarification from the offices and individuals mentioned in the report would be important in establishing the full circumstances surrounding the allegations.

For now, Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo says she remains committed to representing Akwa Ibom students and Nigerian students at large.

**"Aluta Continua! Victoria Ascerta!!"**

*This report is based on a statement issued by Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo. The allegations contained therein represent her account of events and have not been independently verified. Responses from the individuals and offices mentioned were not included in the statement.*

**Source:** Statement by Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo, National Ex-Officio II, NANS National Headquarters.

content:
In a landscape where student leadership is often reduced to titles and visibility, Nene Essien, popularly known as Peculiar Oluwa, is positioning herself differently. As Chairperson of the National Association of University Students Campus Monitoring Committee, Akwa Ibom State Axis, she is currently spearheading the NAUS Campus Tour 2026, a structured statewide engagement initiative focused on student advocacy, representation, and institutional feedback.

This is not a ceremonial visitation exercise. It is a field-based engagement model designed to confront student issues directly within their academic environments and translate feedback into actionable representation.

A Campus Tour Built Around Student Reality

Most student leadership structures operate at a distance from the students they claim to represent. The result is predictable: policies and advocacy efforts shaped by assumption rather than lived experience.

The NAUS Campus Tour 2026 is designed to challenge that gap.

Under Nene Essien’s leadership, the initiative is structured around three operational priorities:

Direct engagement with students across campuses
Documentation of academic and welfare-related concerns
Strengthening communication between student leadership and institutional communities

Rather than centralizing discussions in administrative spaces, the tour shifts engagement to lecture halls, student environments, and campus gathering points. The goal is simple but demanding: replace assumption-driven leadership with feedback-driven action.

Expanding Across Major Universities in Akwa Ibom State
